title: Module sheaves are generated by extension-by-zero free modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ be the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ let $j_U:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal C$ be the localization morphism, $\mathcal O_U$ the restriction of $\mathcal O$ to $\mathcal C/U$, and $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ the extension by zero, so that a section $s\in\mathcal M(U)$ of a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal M$ corresponds to the morphism $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal M$ adjoint to $\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal M|_U$, $1\mapsto s$. Then for every sheaf $\mathcal M$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the coproduct $\bigoplus_{(U,s)}j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$, indexed by the set of pairs $(U,s)$ with $U$ an object of $\mathcal C$ and $s\in\mathcal M(U)$, exists, and the morphism $\bigoplus_{(U,s)}j_{U!}\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal M$ whose $(U,s)$ component is the morphism attached to $s$ is an epimorphism.
